buttonLabel: "Colombia in 7 days: three cities, two flights and the Caribbean Sea"
lead: >-
  In 7 days, this itinerary brings together Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena, along with Lake Guatavita, the Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá, Guatapé and the Rosario Islands. Its 6 nights are divided equally among the three cities, and tickets for the 2 domestic flights are paid for separately. Discover what Medellín adds compared with a five-day trip and how to assess the cost, sightseeing pace and time by the sea.
---

## Colombia in 7 days: why the third city matters

This itinerary reveals 3 different sides of Colombia through [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The capital introduces the history and culture of the Andes; Medellín offers a look at urban transformation and its mountainous surroundings; and Cartagena showcases colonial neighbourhoods and the Caribbean coast.

Unlike the [five-day Bogotá–Cartagena tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/), this itinerary **sets aside 2 days specifically for Medellín and Guatapé**. This is a substantial addition: a tour of city districts and a trip to El Peñón de Guatapé rock. If these places are essential to your travel plans, the seven-day route offers more.

The overnight breakdown is straightforward: 2 nights in Bogotá, 2 in Medellín and 2 in Cartagena. Yet the travel pace is considerably more demanding than the number of days might suggest: you will fly between cities twice, travel to attractions outside the cities and take a boat to the islands.

## The first 2 days: Bogotá, Guatavita and the Salt Cathedral

Your introduction to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) begins with La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection, Bolívar Square and panoramic views from Monserrate. The first day's schedule is fairly full, so allow for your actual arrival time and immigration and airport formalities at El Dorado Airport.

On day two, you leave the capital. The group first travels to [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) and the [town of Guatavita](/colombia/place/guatavita-town/), then visits [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral. This underground complex lies roughly 180 m below ground. Lunch on this excursion is paid for separately.

Two days in the capital region provide a varied introduction to Colombian history, but leave almost no free time. Bogotá is also at a high altitude, so walking immediately after your flight may feel more strenuous. When planning sightseeing on arrival day, consider how you feel and when you actually reach the city.

## Medellín and Guatapé: what the extra 2 days offer

Day 3 includes a Bogotá–Medellín flight and a guided tour of [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), including Comuna 13 and El Castillo Museum. Visiting Comuna 13 introduces the city's contemporary cultural practices, street art and history of change.

The following day takes you to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/). The focus shifts from urban life to a reservoir, mountain views and the brightly painted streets of a small town.

This combination suits travellers seeking more than the architecture of two major cities and a single beach day. However, excursions from Medellín take time: a two-night stay should not be mistaken for two full days of relaxation.

## Cartagena and Rosario: historic streets and the sea

On day 5, the group flies to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The itinerary includes the historic city and San Felipe Fortress. Cartagena is known for its fortifications and colonial architecture, and its historic monuments form part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The next day brings a trip to the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/). The programme includes a private transfer to the pier followed by a shared speedboat to San Pedro de Majagua on [Isla Grande](/colombia/place/isla-grande/). There is time for swimming and relaxation, plus a Caribbean lunch with dessert and a drink. The group returns to Cartagena after lunch.

A private boat can be arranged if you wish, but this is **an additional paid option**. The standard price includes shared sea transport. The beach day does not include an overnight stay on the islands. For several consecutive days of swimming and relaxation, you will need a different itinerary.

## Calculating the full cost: 2 domestic flights are extra

A common mistake when comparing itineraries is to look only at the minimum tour price and overlook intercity airfares. Here, **both the Bogotá–Medellín and Medellín–Cartagena flights are paid for separately**, as is the international flight. Private ground transfers included in the itinerary are covered.

The service price covers 6 hotel nights, daily breakfasts, excursions with an **English-speaking guide**, and an island day including a shared boat, lunch, dessert, coffee or tea and the maritime fee. Other lunches, dinners, tips and individual activities are additional expenses.

Prices depend on hotel category and room occupancy. The minimum price of **$2829** is for **DBL accommodation in 4★ hotels**; in the same category SGL costs $5372 and TRP costs $2861. A different rate schedule applies to 5★ hotels. When comparing this with the five-day tour, compare equivalent room arrangements and account for the number of domestic flights.

| Feature | Seven-day itinerary |
|---|---|
| Overnight stays | 2 + 2 + 2 across three cities |
| Domestic flights | 2; tickets paid separately |
| Main sightseeing language | English |
| Island transport | Shared speedboat |
| Time by the sea | 1 excursion day |

## When to choose 5 days and when to choose 7

**5 days** are enough if your main aim is to see the capital, Guatavita and Cartagena, plus one trip to the Rosario Islands. The **7-day** option adds a dedicated programme in Medellín and Guatapé. It gives a more varied overview of Colombia, with additional costs and travel.

If history and architecture are your priorities, also explore [cultural journeys in Colombia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/). If you want more time on the coast, one island excursion day may not be enough: compare other [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/) and how many nights they actually spend by the sea.

## Frequently asked questions about the 7-day Colombia tour

### How many domestic flights are included in the itinerary?

Two: Bogotá–Medellín and Medellín–Cartagena. Both air tickets are paid for separately from the ground services.

### Do we visit Guatapé and El Peñón rock?

Yes. One full excursion day is set aside for a trip from Medellín to Guatapé and El Peñón de Guatapé.

### How many days are available for beach relaxation?

The Rosario Islands have 1 excursion day. Overnight stays are in Cartagena rather than on the islands.

### Is a Russian-speaking guide available?

The quoted programme includes English-speaking guiding. Any other language must be agreed when booking; it is not automatically included.

### What is the main difference from the 5-day tour?

Medellín, Comuna 13, Guatapé and an additional domestic flight have been added. Bogotá, Guatavita, Cartagena and the island day feature in both programmes.

## Colombia in 12 days: sightseeing and relaxation on San Andrés Island

**This tour is for travellers who want to discover Colombia and enjoy a proper break by the Caribbean Sea.** The programme spans 12 days and 11 nights. City and nature excursions come first, followed by **three free days on San Andrés Island**. After the island, the journey continues through Medellín and the area around Bogotá.

Unlike short introductory routes, this trip includes the [coffee region near Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) and the Caribbean coast. It is important to distinguish days without scheduled excursions from those with activities planned throughout the day.

If time at the sea matters more to you than a long list of cultural stops, San Andrés is the strongest reason to choose this tour. If you primarily want to delve deeper into Colombia's history or hike in Tayrona, compare the [14-day journey to Santa Marta](/colombia/tour/iconic-colombia-14-days/).

## Why San Andrés Island changes the nature of the trip

After [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), you fly to [San Andrés](/colombia/place/san-andres/). Days 6, 7 and 8 are reserved for seaside relaxation, with no compulsory sightseeing tour scheduled for each of those days.

You can set your own pace, spend a day at the beach, take walks and enjoy the island's facilities. Extra marine activities should be assessed on their actual terms: simply being available at the destination does not mean that they are included in the package.

San Andrés offers a different experience from Cartagena. In Cartagena, sightseeing centres on the city walls and old town; on the island, the focus is beach relaxation. According to Colombia's official tourism portal, the island is known for its warm Caribbean waters, although weather varies by season. Before departure, check the local tourist-card, flight and baggage requirements.

## What the coffee region adds near the start

Day two includes a flight to [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/) and visits to [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/). After a large high-altitude city, you find yourself among the green slopes and wax palms for which this region is known.

The next day is dedicated to the coffee valley and activities, including a canopy tour. Coffee culture in the western Andes is rooted in plantations, small farms and local communities. This section is different from a single visit to a hacienda outside Bogotá: the journey actually passes through a region where coffee production and rural mountain life are central to the local culture.

If coffee is your primary interest, compare specialised trips in the [coffee tours section](/interests/coffee-tours/). Coffee is an important part of this twelve-day itinerary, but the trip then moves on to the sea, major cities and other excursions.

## How sightseeing and leisure days fit together

| Stage | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Bogotá and Pereira | Capital history, coffee, Cocora |
| Cartagena and San Andrés | Old town and 3 days by the sea |
| Medellín and final excursion | Guatapé, Guatavita, Zipaquirá |

In the city section, [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) introduces historic neighbourhoods, museums and Monserrate. In [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), the itinerary includes colonial architecture, fortification walls and city districts.

After San Andrés, travellers arrive in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) and then visit [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñón rock. Near the end, there is an excursion to [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) and the [Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/).

This order involves several domestic flights and changes of hotel. Airport days should not be treated as full free days: travel and check-in procedures significantly reduce the time available for walks and exploration.

## What is included and what to arrange yourself

The tour includes hotel accommodation, transfers, excursions with a Russian-speaking guide and **domestic flights**. Expenses not included comprise optional excursions, food and drinks outside the included meal plan, tips and personal spending.

The journey spans different climates: high-altitude Bogotá, the green hills of coffee country and warm Caribbean destinations. Comfortable shoes and rain protection are useful for sightseeing, while light clothing and sun protection are important on the island. Check flight conditions and baggage limits across all domestic sectors before packing.

The itinerary combines active days, such as the canopy experience and the trip to the rock, with leisurely time on the island. **The San Andrés break offsets the busy schedule only in the middle of the journey**: the final days are full of sightseeing and transfers again. Consider whether you enjoy this alternation when choosing the trip.

## Frequently asked questions about the San Andrés tour

### How many beach days are free of scheduled excursions?

There are three free days on San Andrés. Travel time for flights to and from the island is counted separately.

### Does the itinerary visit coffee plantations?

The coffee region is included via Pereira, Salento and the Cocora Valley. For specific coffee-related activities, consult this tour's programme and the [coffee tours section](/interests/coffee-tours/).

### Are domestic flights included?

Yes. They are listed among this programme's included services. International flight arrangements and additional expenses should be checked separately.

### Is this a good route for visiting Tayrona National Park?

[Tayrona National Park](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/) is not part of this twelve-day programme. It is visited on the [14-day route via Santa Marta](/colombia/tour/iconic-colombia-14-days/).

## Colombia Live: from the Andes to the Caribbean in 13 days

This journey has four successive parts: historic highlands, coffee country, coastal nature and colonial Cartagena. **The route suits travellers who want to experience several Colombian regions in one visit and are comfortable with multiple transfers.** The programme lasts 13 days and 12 nights, with arrival and departure days included in the total duration.

You begin in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and [Villa de Leyva](/colombia/place/villa-de-leyva/), then head towards [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/) and its coffee farms. The Caribbean part takes you through [Santa Marta](/colombia/place/santa-marta/), [Tayrona National Park](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/) and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). This is a geographically extensive journey, making flight sequences and rest periods between active days especially important.

## What each section of the journey offers

| Part of the journey | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Bogotá and the highlands | Museums and colonial towns |
| Coffee region | Plantations and wax palms |
| Santa Marta and Tayrona | Hiking trail and Caribbean Sea |
| Cartagena | Fortress, bay and cuisine |

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), sightseeing includes La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection and a coffee tasting. This is followed by a visit to the Salt Cathedral in [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/), historic [Villa de Leyva](/colombia/place/villa-de-leyva/) and its surroundings. One of these excursions lasts approximately 12 hours. If you find long car journeys tiring, discuss this part in advance.

Near [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), the programme visits [Filandia](/colombia/place/filandia/), [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/). Here a walk through cloud forest introduces you to the Quindío wax palm. Another day is devoted to a coffee farm in [Santa Rosa de Cabal](/colombia/place/santa-rosa-de-cabal/), where you learn about planting, harvesting, drying and roasting the beans. Coffee becomes an experience in its own right, although the tour's overall scope is broader.

On the coast, a city tour of [Santa Marta](/colombia/place/santa-marta/) and a full day in [Tayrona](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/) are planned, including a walk to Cabo San Juan. In [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), the programme includes a sunset cruise on the bay, the historic centre and a visit to a fishing village, where residents introduce guests to their livelihoods and the preparation of the catch.

## Travel time and the tour's activity level

Moving between regions requires **two domestic flights: Bogotá–Pereira and Pereira–Santa Marta**. Both flights are paid for separately from the included services. The journey between Santa Marta and Cartagena is by road and takes approximately 4 hours.

The most demanding parts are the highland excursion via Zipaquirá and Villa de Leyva, the nature walk in the Cocora Valley and the day in Tayrona. The Tayrona excursion is planned for about 10 hours including transport and walking. Elsewhere, city tours alternate with time at hotels. If you prefer a journey with very little walking or long-distance travel, compare shorter [Colombia itineraries](/colombia/tour/).

## What is included and what costs extra

The trip includes 12 nights of accommodation: 2 in Bogotá, 1 in Villa de Leyva, 3 in Pereira, 3 in Santa Marta and 3 in Cartagena. Also included are 12 breakfasts, 5 lunches, specified ground transfers and guided excursion services.

Most city and coffee excursions are private. **The Tayrona visit, bay cruise and fishing-village experience are described as group activities.** This distinction matters for expectations about pace and fellow participants. International and domestic air tickets, tips, personal expenses and certain fees are excluded. A separate pier fee is specified for the bay cruise; consult the specific tour listing for the final terms and prices.

## Choosing dates for both the coast and the highlands

You will encounter very different conditions. Bring clothing suitable for cooler weather and possible rain in Andean cities; comfortable shoes and rain protection for Pereira; and light clothing, a hat and beach essentials for the Caribbean. In Tayrona, priorities include comfortable long-distance walking, water and compliance with the protected area's rules.

**Tayrona regularly closes for agreed periods of ecological rest and Indigenous community activities.** Access to particular sectors may also change temporarily. Before fixing your dates, check the official park portal for entry conditions and the day's actual tour schedule. Tayrona's presence in the itinerary does not guarantee access to every trail on every calendar date.

## Who might prefer another itinerary

If coffee and the natural landscapes of the Andes are your main interests, [Colombia Coffee](/colombia/tour/colombia-coffee/) focuses on plantations, Salento and Cocora in a shorter trip. For an introduction primarily to urban life in Bogotá and Medellín, consider [Metropolitan Colombia](/colombia/tour/metropolitan-colombia/). Choose Colombia Live for the full journey from the Andes to the Caribbean, continuing through Tayrona and Cartagena.

## Frequently asked questions about Colombia Live

### Can we travel without domestic flights?

The itinerary includes flights from Bogotá to Pereira and from Pereira to Santa Marta. They are paid for separately. Changing the transport arrangements would alter the original programme and should be discussed individually.

### Is there time for the beach?

Yes. The day in Tayrona National Park includes a visit to Cabo San Juan and free time by the sea. Swimming is permitted only where park rules and local safety conditions allow it.

### Are all excursions private?

No. Alongside private city and coffee experiences, the tour includes group visits to Tayrona, a Cartagena bay cruise and the fishing-village programme.

### Do I need hiking experience?

No sporting qualification is specified for the tour, but the Cocora Valley and Tayrona require you to be comfortable walking on natural trails in hot or rainy weather. Agree on the pace and any possible adjustments before booking.

## Colombia VIP in 10 days: culture, coffee and 3 nights on Barú Island

The main distinction of this journey is its combination of in-depth Andean excursions and a proper Caribbean coastal break. The route includes 3 nights in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), 1 in the [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/) region, 2 in [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and 3 on [Barú Island](/colombia/place/baru-island/). There is time for city history, coffee culture and several relaxed days by the sea.

The programme includes private transfers, excursions in the agreed guiding languages and selected hotels. However, read the precise list of included services: the VIP label itself does not mean every extra activity or flight is covered by the price.

## Bogotá: museums, Monserrate and highland history

On arrival, accommodation is planned at Four Seasons Casa Medina in Bogotá. The city stands around 2600 metres above sea level, so it is helpful to allow some rest after your flight. The following day takes you through La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, Casa de la Moneda, the Botero Museum and Bolívar Square before continuing to Monserrate.

Museum opening schedules impose restrictions: the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays, while Casa de la Moneda and the Botero Museum are closed on Tuesdays. The order of visits is adjusted to your actual dates so that you do not miss a key part of the cultural itinerary.

Another excursion combines [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) with [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral. It takes approximately 9 hours, including transfers and walks. Lunch is not included that day. This is one of the longest days in the first part of the journey.

## Coffee region: Cocora Valley, Salento and El Ocaso farm

After flying to Pereira, you travel to the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) to see wax palms and visit [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/). The next experience is a dedicated [tour of El Ocaso coffee farm](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/).

At the farm, visitors learn how coffee plants are cultivated, how cherries are picked by hand, and how the beans are processed, dried, roasted and tasted. This is ideal for those who want to understand where Colombian coffee's flavours and characteristics originate, rather than simply stopping at a café. Similar experiences are featured in the [coffee tours section](/interests/coffee-tours/).

After a busy day, accommodation is planned at Visus Hotel Boutique & Spa. Early the following morning, there is a **hot-air balloon flight over the coffee valley**. It is included in the paid services. Canopy activities, horse riding and a barista show, by contrast, require separate arrangements and are not confirmed as included. A second breakfast after the flight costs extra.

Because you also fly to Cartagena that day, extra activities should only be added after checking the airport departure time.

## Cartagena and Barú: two different ways to enjoy the Caribbean

In [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), accommodation is planned at Sofitel Legend Santa Clara, along with a city tour of La Popa hill, San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, historic streets and bastions, Getsemaní district and Las Bóvedas artisan centre. Cartagena's port fortifications are UNESCO World Heritage-listed, making its historic areas especially rewarding to explore.

A speedboat then takes you to [Barú](/colombia/place/baru-island/). Accommodation is at Las Islas in a bungalow with a private pool. With 3 nights on the island, this stay is much more than a short excursion from Cartagena.

You can combine the beach, walks and relaxation with additional activities. Diving, kayaking and a trip to the Enchanted Lagoon are listed as possibilities, but their costs and conditions must be agreed separately. If a calm seaside finale is your main objective, this stage distinguishes the route from more fast-paced Colombian journeys.

## Hotels, flights and the final price

Accommodation is planned at Four Seasons Casa Medina (Bogotá), Visus Hotel Boutique & Spa (Pereira), Sofitel Legend Santa Clara (Cartagena) and Las Islas (Barú). Room categories and hotel availability are confirmed for specific dates; equivalent substitutions are permitted under the tour conditions.

Included services cover accommodation with breakfasts, private individual transfers, excursions with Russian-speaking guides in Bogotá and Pereira and an English-speaking guide in Cartagena, specified admission fees, the hot-air balloon flight and the Cartagena–Barú–Cartagena boat journey.

**International tickets and the domestic Bogotá–Pereira and Pereira–Cartagena flights are paid for separately.** Personal expenses, most lunches and dinners, and unconfirmed optional activities also cost extra. There is no published fixed price for this VIP journey: the final amount depends on dates, accommodation and agreed options.

To compare formats, consider the [8-day trip to Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena](/colombia/tour/colombia-capitals/) and the [12-day journey to Caño Cristales](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-beyond/). The first focuses more on cities, the second on the natural area of La Macarena. This VIP programme centres on the coffee farm and an extended stay on Barú.

## Frequently asked questions about the VIP Colombia tour

### How does this tour differ from the three-city itinerary?

It includes a dedicated coffee-farm visit, a hot-air balloon flight and 3 nights on Barú Island. The three-city journey includes Medellín and Guatapé instead.

### Are the canopy activity and horse riding included?

No. Their conditions and prices must be arranged separately. The hot-air balloon flight is included in the core services.

### Is there enough time for a proper beach break?

Yes. The stay on Barú lasts 3 nights following two nights in Cartagena. Extra water activities are arranged separately.

### Can I know the final price in advance?

Yes. It is calculated based on the chosen dates and confirmed rooms. No fixed price is published, and domestic and international flights are not included in the main price.

## Colombia in 14 days: five stops and the Caribbean coast

**This itinerary suits travellers who want to experience Colombia's contrasts in one journey and enjoy frequent changes of scenery.** It lasts 14 days and 13 nights: 3 nights each in Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena, 2 in Pereira and 2 in Santa Marta.

The main feature is more than a sequence of large cities. Between them, you visit [coffee farms around Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) and [Tayrona National Park](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/). The combination is particularly appealing to people interested in culture, nature, walking and local culinary traditions.

Unlike the [12-day itinerary with three free days on San Andrés](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-beaches-12-days/), this journey involves far more sightseeing. There are short stops by the sea and dedicated nature excursions rather than a beach holiday based on one island.

## Why the itinerary passes through these regions

| Stop | Main experiences |
|---|---|
| Bogotá | History, Monserrate, Guatavita |
| Medellín | Comuna 13, El Peñol, Guatapé |
| Pereira | Coffee farm, Cocora |
| Cartagena | Old town, bay, Rosario |
| Santa Marta | City history and Tayrona |

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), you visit the Gold Museum, historic La Candelaria and Monserrate. An excursion outside the capital combines the [Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/). This is the high-altitude part of the journey, where elevation and weather differ from the Caribbean coast.

In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), you explore contemporary urban culture through Comuna 13, parks and Botero sculptures. A separate excursion takes you to El Peñol rock and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), known for its painted façades and reservoirs.

Next comes the coffee region. A farm near Pereira introduces the processing, drying and roasting of coffee beans. In [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), the experience shifts to hiking among wax palms. The Coffee Cultural Landscape of the western Andes is recognised as UNESCO heritage, although excursions on this tour follow the specified route rather than every attraction in the wider region.

## How the Caribbean days differ: Cartagena, Rosario and Tayrona

In [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), the itinerary includes the historic centre, San Felipe de Barajas Fortress and an evening trip on the bay. A sea excursion to the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) follows, with a beach stop. This is **a day trip with a return to the mainland**, not several nights on the islands.

From Cartagena, the route continues to [Santa Marta](/colombia/place/santa-marta/) with a private ground transfer lasting approximately four hours. In Santa Marta itself, sightseeing introduces the historic centre and places associated with Simón Bolívar.

One of the most active days is the visit to [Tayrona National Park](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/). The itinerary includes a hike from the Cañaveral sector via Arrecifes to Cabo San Juan. Part of the route follows ecological trails, followed by time at the sea and the return hike. Approximately 10 hours are allocated to the excursion.

**Tayrona requires readiness for a lengthy walk in tropical conditions.** This distinguishes it from the Rosario boat trip and a relaxed beach day. Trail availability and park visiting arrangements should be checked before travelling, as they depend on current rules and natural conditions.

## Guiding arrangements and additional costs

The tour combines different excursion formats: private city experiences and some group marine and nature activities. English- and Spanish-speaking guides accompany different stages. **Do not assume that a Russian-speaking guide will accompany you for all 14 days:** no such overall provision is stated.

Included are accommodation in five cities, ground transfers, 13 breakfasts, 4 lunches and the scheduled excursions. However, **international and domestic air tickets are explicitly listed as excluded**. When comparing budgets, therefore, consider not only the programme price but also separate flights, fees and other exclusions.

Transfers across Bogotá, Medellín, Pereira, Cartagena and Santa Marta occupy a significant part of the journey. Distinguish flight days from full sightseeing days, and avoid scheduling another demanding activity on the evening after the Tayrona hike.

This itinerary suits travellers interested in architecture, city life, [coffee traditions](/interests/coffee-tours/) and Colombian nature. For a quieter Caribbean holiday with several free days, compare [all Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/) and the San Andrés option.

## Frequently asked questions about the 14-day Colombia tour

### Does it visit an actual coffee farm rather than just offer a tasting?

Yes. Near Pereira, the itinerary includes a farm visit demonstrating bean harvesting, processing, drying and roasting. The following day is dedicated to Salento and the Cocora Valley.

### How long does the Tayrona visit take?

Approximately 10 hours are allocated to the entire park visit, walking and return journey. It is a considerably more active day than a typical city excursion.

### Are domestic air tickets included in the price?

No. International and domestic air tickets are listed among the expenses paid for separately on this 14-day tour.

### Are all excursions private and led by Russian-speaking guides?

No. Formats and languages vary by location. Some excursions are private and others are group activities, with guiding in English and Spanish.
